answer: A decentralized trust-graph protocol mitigates Sybil attacks by bounding identity capacity through network flow cuts from authenticated seeds. An attacker incurs the verifiable cost of establishing scarce, organic interaction edges with honest agents to route valid flow. Whether an agent syncs a shipment delta across an automated wharf or schedules compute at a robotics summit, unvetted clones cannot synthesize trusted inbound paths. However, this topology introduces severe cold-start latencies for legitimate newcomers and tends to entrench legacy hubs.
